# Sirach Chapter 46 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalent)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 46 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**46:1** Joshua son of Nun was a warrior without peer — Moses' successor in the prophetic role. His very name announced what he was: a great salvation for God's chosen people. He waged war against the enemies who rose against them and gave Israel its inheritance.

**46:2** What a glorious sight when he raised his hand and swung his sword against city after city!

**46:3** No one before him had ever stood so firm — because he himself was waging the Lord's wars.

**46:4** Was it not through him that the sun stood still, and one day stretched to the length of two?

**46:5** When enemies closed in on him from every side, he cried out to the Most High, the Mighty One — and the great Lord answered him with a storm of mighty hailstones.

**46:6** He swept through a nation in battle; on the descent he annihilated his opponents. The nations learned what his armor was: he fought with the Lord before him, following the Mighty One.

**46:7** Back in the days of Moses, he and Caleb son of Jephunneh had shown faithful loyalty — standing firm against the entire congregation, holding the people back from sin, silencing their wicked grumbling.

**46:8** Of six hundred thousand foot soldiers, only those two were preserved to lead the people into their inheritance — a land flowing with milk and honey.

**46:9** The Lord gave Caleb strength that lasted into his old age, so that he climbed into the hill country and his descendants received it as their inheritance,

**46:10** so that all Israel could see for themselves how good it is to follow the Lord.

**46:11** And the judges — each one by name — all those who never gave their hearts to idols and never turned away from the Lord — may their memory be blessed!

**46:12** May their bones sprout new life from where they lie; may the names of those honored men live on in their sons.

**46:13** Samuel was beloved of his Lord. A prophet of the Lord, he established the kingdom and anointed rulers over his people.

**46:14** By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord kept watch over Jacob.

**46:15** His faithfulness proved him a true prophet; by his words he was trusted as a reliable seer.

**46:16** When enemies surrounded him on every side, he called on the Lord, the Mighty One, as he offered a suckling lamb.

**46:17** And the Lord thundered from heaven; his mighty voice rang out with a great crash.

**46:18** He crushed the leaders of the enemy and destroyed all the Philistine rulers.

**46:19** Just before his eternal rest, Samuel called the Lord and his anointed to witness: "I have taken no man's property — not so much as a sandal." And no one accused him.

**46:20** And even after he had fallen asleep, he prophesied — he announced the king's death, lifted his voice from the earth to prophesy, and blotted out the wickedness of the people.
